etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English obstinat(e) (“obstinate, stubborn”), from Latin obstinātus, perfect passive participle of obstinō (“set one's mind firmly upon, resolve”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from ob (“before”) + *stinare, from stare (“to stand”). Doublet of ostinato.
senses: Stubbornly adhering to an opinion, purpose, or course, usually with implied unreasonableness; persistent.
Of an inanimate object, not easily subdued or removed.
